text:
harper: noticed SCIM deprovision spike ~12% failures since 09:05 UTC, mostly 403/KMS AccessDenied. Anyone touching RBAC or service principals?
leo: I deployed a principal rename in the team-mapping job at 09:00 — svc principal changed from arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/scim-old to arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/scim-new
annis: that will definitely break KMS if the key policy wasn't updated. Can you paste the exact KMS error from the provisioner logs?
leo: log excerpt: 
```
2026-06-10T09:04:59Z ERROR scim: decrypt extID failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222333444555:key/ef12-3456
```
annis: yep that's a key policy deny. KMS doesn't return details beyond AccessDenied so deprovs get retried and become orphaned.
harper: opening incident INC-2026-4412 and paging eng-platform + SRE
oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-4412 "SCIM deprov KMS denies after principal rotation"
leo: can someone add the new role to the key policy? I missed that step.
annis: I'll update the key policy and then we need to restart the provisioner to clear cached contexts. Also keep the old role for a 24h grace window.
infra-bot: applied key policy change at 09:12 UTC, both ARNs present.
annis: rolling restart scim-provisioner now -> kubectl rollout restart deployment/scim-provisioner -n idp
leo: after restart, retries start to succeed, sample: 
```
2026-06-10T09:15:21Z INFO scim: decrypt succeeded, deprovisioned svcacc-42
```
harper: run a backfill for the 08:55-09:12 window and watch for any remaining failures. Also create follow-ups: RBAC rename checklist to include KMS key policy step, and CI lint to detect principal/ARN diffs vs key policies.
oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-4412 resolved -> root cause: principal rename not added to KMS key policy; fix: updated policy, restarted provisioner, backfilled missed deprovisions.
